recentItems.title: Bukele's El Salvador Soldier Killed In Haiti As Mercenaries Fled? Inside Port-Au-Prince 'GANG WAR'
recentItems.description:
Bukele's El Salvador Soldier Killed In Haiti As Mercenaries Fled? Inside Port-Au-Prince 'GANG WAR'

In El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele has identified the three soldiers from the Central American country who recently died in Haiti as they fight violent gangs, asserting one of them stepped in after private contractors allegedly abandoned their positions.
Among the contractors working in Haiti are those with Vectus Global, a private security firm founded by former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince.
Bukele did not say which operation the Salvadoran troops were involved. However, forces in recent days have been fighting powerful gangs entrenched in Martissant, a community located in a key corridor that links Haiti’s capital to the country’s western and southern regions.
It is the first major operation in Martissant in the more than five years that gangs have controlled it.
Bukele pledged $200,000 and a monthly income to each soldier’s family and said troops wishing to leave Haiti could return without reprisals.

recentItems.title: Houthis Hit Riyadh’s Tallest Skyscraper 2nd Time In A Week In Fresh Attack? Saudi Panics? Yemen War
recentItems.description:
Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, which houses the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), has reportedly been hit for the second time in less than a week. Three separate witnesses told AFP that an unspecified projectile struck the tower in the capital's business district.

In this video we break down what has been reported so far, why this landmark matters so much to the Saudi economy, what is still unknown about who or what is behind the strikes, and what it could mean for the Yemen war and the wider Gulf region.

No official confirmation or attacker has been named yet, and we will update as more details emerge.
